name: Johan Vega
life: “I still remember taking two buses to the home across the valley.” Sunday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Johan stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I can swap two calls and cover one dinner. Somebody needs to count the extra bus fare.
appearance: Johan has a center part and straight chestnut hair, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with one cuff folded back twice. When somebody else has the floor, Johan draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
personality: Johan has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To pay for the extra journey behind a shift swap.
family: Annette Alder is Johan’s stepsibling. Johan can always ask for five minutes alone. Annette asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The quiet verse*, Annette says, “I conduct the choir. My instinct was to fill the space and I practiced keeping my hands down.”
connections: Remy Knight. An extra dinner trip puts a worker who recognizes the client's hand beside the plate.

reactions.situation: Someone asks a family member to translate an intimate question
reactions.response: Johan offers a qualified interpreter and lets the client decide how much family should hear.

reactions.situation: A customer is short at the till while a queue forms
reactions.response: Johan offers the shortfall once and accepts the answer, including a refusal.

reactions.response: Johan explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
